title: look.toml
description:
How Banda looks and sounds: the theme, tiles, columns, font, motion,
sounds and calls. A theme's `banda.toml` takes the same keys.

theme.description: `"omarchy"`, `"banda"`, a theme's name, or `{ light, dark }`.

radius.description: shadcn's `--radius`, in pixels: every corner is a step of it.

hyprland.description: Whether to take Hyprland's rounding, border and gaps.

colors.description: Palette entries over the theme's: a palette name or hex.

tokens.description:
Tokens over the derived ones, by their names without `--`: a palette
name, a token's name or any CSS colour.

desk.description: The desk the tiles float over (ADR 0023).

notify.description: How Banda tells its Person of a call (ADR 0011, decision 7).

Desk.description: The desk: the bar, and the space around and between the tiles.

glass.description:
Glass: the desk shows the wallpaper behind it, blurred. Off, the
desk is solid.

material.description:
`"banda"`: Banda draws the glass itself, from the wallpaper, the
same everywhere. `"system"`: the system's own material, vibrancy on
macOS and acrylic on Windows 11, or on Linux the compositor's blur
of the desktop; it shows from Banda's next start. Unset, the
platform's: the system's on macOS and Windows, Banda's on Linux
(ADR 0030).

wallpaper.description:
The picture Banda's glass is made of: a path, `~/` for home. With
neither this nor `wallpaper-dark` set, the desktop's own wallpaper:
Omarchy's, GNOME's and its family's, KDE's, XFCE's or hyprpaper's
(ADR 0030).

wallpaper-dark.description:
The picture for when Banda is dark, the same way; when one of the
two is set, it is the picture for both. With neither set, the
desktop's own dark wallpaper when it keeps one (GNOME and KDE do).

blur.description: How frosted Banda's glass is: the blur's radius, in pixels.

saturation.description:
How vivid the wallpaper's colours stay under the glass: 1 as they
are, more is richer, 0 is grey.

grain.description:
A fine grain over the glass, from 0 (none) to 1, so it reads as a
material rather than a blurred photo.

opacity.description:
The desk's tint over the blurred desktop, from 0 (clear) to 1
(solid), with glass on: unset, 0.1 on macOS and Windows, whose
material is tinted already, and 0.4 on Linux.

sidebar.description:
`"panel"`: the sidebar floats as a glass panel. `"desk"`: its rows
sit right on the desk.

sidebar-shadow.description:
The shadow the sidebar's panel casts on a glass desk, from 0 (none)
to 1 (the darkest).

SidebarStyle.description: How the sidebar sits on the desk.

dim-inactive.description:
How much the tiles without the focus darken, from 0 to 1, as
Hyprland's `dim_inactive` and `dim_strength`.

opacity.description:
How solid a tile is over a glass desk, from 0 to 1: 1 is solid.
Without glass the tiles are solid.

shadow.description:
The shadow a tile casts on a glass desk, from 0 (none) to 1 (the
darkest).

Corner.description: A corner: a step of shadcn's ladder, or pixels.

ring.description:
niri's focus ring: how far the focused tile's frame grows out
into the gap, so nothing moves. It is the border's own colour, one
frame and not two. 0 draws none.

workspaces.description:
How the bar shows the workspaces: `"numbers"`, or `"dots"` with the
one shown drawn long, as GNOME's.

Workspaces.description: How the bar shows the workspaces.

Drawer.description: The drawer: a Thread that drops from the top over the workspace.

height.description:
How far down it drops: a share of the room under the bar, from 0
to 1.

harness.description:
The Harness its Thread starts on, as `"claude"`; this computer's
first one when left out.

off.description: Turns every event off, as the system's reduced motion does.

slowdown.description: 2 is twice as slow; 0.5 twice as fast.

strip.description: Scrolling the Strip to a column.

move.description:
Columns going to their new places, when one opens, closes, moves or
changes its width.

open.description: A tile coming in: it fades in, growing from half its size.

close.description: A tile going: it fades out, shrinking to four fifths, as the rest close in.

Event.description: One event's table: `off`, and a `spring` or an `easing`.

damping-ratio.description: 1 comes to rest without overshooting; less bounces.

stiffness.description: How hard it pulls: more is faster.

epsilon.description: How close, as a share of the way, counts as there.

curve.description: A named curve or `cubic-bezier(x1, y1, x2, y2)`.

presets.description: What Alt+Ctrl+Left and Right step through.

heights.description:
What Alt+Shift+R and Alt+Ctrl+Up and Down step a Pane's height
through, as shares of its column.

default.description: A new column's width, where its Pane does not ask for its own.

alone.description:
The width of a column alone on its workspace, until the Person
gives it one: once a second opens beside it, both take `default`.

display.description: How a new column shows its Panes, as niri's `default-column-display`.

min.description: The narrowest a column is drawn, in rem; a list's is half of it.

snap.description:
How near, in pixels, a size dragged with the mouse holds at a
preset or a height; 0 never.

Center.description: Where the Strip scrolls a focused column to.

oneOf.description: The least scroll that shows it whole.
The middle, when it does not fit beside the column focused before.

Display.description: How a column shows its Panes.

oneOf.description: One above another, sharing the column's height.

One at a time, the rest as tabs over it, as niri's tabbed column and
Hyprland's group.

size.description:
The interface's usual text, in pixels; everything measured in text
grows with it, as with a zoom.

SoundSettings.description: `[sound]` as one layer says it: every key optional.

room.description: A soft room around each sound.

Families.description: The family every call comes from, or `off` for silence.

Call.description: One call: on, off, or a family to borrow this one sound from.

Family.description: A family of Banda's sounds; each plays every call its own way.

NotifySettings.description: `[notify]` as one layer says it: every key optional.

system.description: When a call becomes a system notification.

window.description: When a call becomes a toast in the window.

detail.description: What the Thread said, in the words; false shows only its title.

done.description: Whether a Thread that finished tells you.

asking.description: Whether a Thread that asks you something tells you.

failed.description: Whether a Thread that failed tells you.

problems.description:
Whether something new that broke in Banda itself tells you, with
no sound (ADR 0039).

System.description: When a call becomes a system notification.

oneOf.description: When the window is not in front.
Always, instead of a toast too.

Toasts.description: When a call becomes a toast in the window.

oneOf.description: For a thing whose Pane is not on screen.
The desktop's: nothing but the Marks while its Do Not Disturb is on.
None: Banda tells its Person regardless.
